pr_title: Improve the editor template workflow for users and devs
pr_body:
_Co-Authored-By: jmb462 <jmb462@gmail.com>_

This PR attempts to improve/rewrite the script template workflow to make the usage as easy/smooth as possible.

Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/3365

fix #36605
fix #28799
fix #44534
fix #46436
close https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/1899

![1_before-after](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6397893/137722565-a47c204b-1b81-47bd-8df8-7a0d1be83903.png)

## What are the main changes?

- Built-in templates are in external file instead of hard-coded c++, they are no more mixed with user templates and can be updated
- Templates are now linked to a node, when you create a script for a node, you will only see the templates for this node, or one of its parents.
- Simplification and cleaning.

## How it can be used by core dev ##

The original motivation was to provide a more relevant template for CharacterBody nodes in order to :
    - help to avoid the common error we see in issues (like forget to assign the result of move and slide in 3.x)
    - help to make the transition in 4.0 (act like a tutorial)
    - fast prototyping, you have a moving character in few seconds

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6397893/137722735-84901d90-f322-4898-a986-0cb8129903c5.mp4

## How it works?

The template folders have the following structure

![2_structure](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6397893/137722777-6a55260a-f4df-486b-ad06-fa71ab535183.png)

To add a template simply create a file in the correct folder (`template_path/node_type/file.ext`), that's it.

By default:
 - the name of the template file will be the name of the file
 - the description will be empty
 - the space indent will be 4
 - the template will not be use as default
 
You can customize the template info with metas at the begning of your templates. Metas starts with the single-line comment syntax of your language:

```
# meta-name: Basic movement
# meta-description: Classic movement for gravity games (platformer, ...)
# meta-default: true
# meta-space-indent: 4
```

Example of description:

![Screenshot 2021-10-18 at 14 40 43](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6397893/137732515-827f6401-88df-4a9f-a9ae-d83ef9635363.png)

**It works exactly the same for built-in and user templates**

## Notes

- When you create an editor plugin in c# you will have the basic structure for a plugin that I found in the doc. However there is a warning that pop up for now (I don't know why as I don't use c# & there was nothing before)
- I wonder if the **project** template folder should not be fixed like the add-ons one (not changeable in the editor), to avoid the ifdef in `gdscript.cpp`
pr_comments:
> the space indent will be 4

As per the [GDScript style guide](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/getting_started/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_styleguide.html), indentation should use tabs by default. Or is this about templates being written with spaces instead of tabs (to convert from spaces to tabs)?

Official script templates should be indented with tabs, still.

Not sure from the changes if you handle this or not, but I think templates at the root of the template folder (like now) can be handled as Object or Node templates for backward compatibility.

PS. Also, did you call the two files basic_mouv on purpose? Looks like a typo, and we better use full qualified names in the engine anyway.

> As per the GDScript style guide, indentation should use tabs by default. Or is this about templates being written with spaces instead of tabs (to convert from spaces to tabs)? Official script templates should be indented with tabs, still.

The parser will replace the tab and 4 spaces by `_TS_` (previously `%TS%`) by default. If the user want to use 2 spaces indent in the templates; he can pass the information in the parser with this meta. The result will look like this:

![Screenshot 2021-10-18 at 15 26 00](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6397893/137740397-33932935-7cfe-4a14-9300-bef3fdcc8022.png)

In the end, the result of the indentation will be the one defined in the editor's configuration:

![Screenshot 2021-10-18 at 15 23 37](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6397893/137740151-651ead27-3f4a-41d6-bbf8-57ecd98dc10a.png)

> So is the replacement syntax changed from `%BASE%` to `_BASE_`? Is there a reason to use `_` over `%`? It seems to me that `_` could be conflicting with valid scripts.

@raulsntos  Yes, if you use `% %`syntax you will have errors in your editor (godot or external) when you open/edit the template as this syntax is not allowed in the language:

Godot:
![Screenshot 2021-10-18 at 18 18 40](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6397893/137770119-db0783d5-222f-47e0-b71a-45b91681723d.png)
VS Code:
![Screenshot 2021-10-17 at 11 37 20](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6397893/137770189-20b7e70d-7ae2-467f-a50e-56ef2c1c3ad8.png)

To avoid this I changed the syntax to a valid one. As this syntax only concerns templates, I don't think is an issue, it seems to me the lesser evil.

![Screenshot 2021-10-17 at 11 37 32](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6397893/137770929-239cc0cc-299a-4490-a9f5-aa28894aae9e.png)
Good enough for me, I guess the chances of someone wanting to use a world like `_CLASS_` in the output of the template are low.
I thought about doubling the underscore at one point `__BASE__`, then I thought that one was enough. But if anyone has a better idea, I'll take it.

> Not sure from the changes if you handle this or not, but I think templates at the root of the template folder (like now) can be handled as Object or Node templates for backward compatibility.

I'm working with @fabriceci on this PR.
Following your comments, I've started implementing this, but I realized that it brings more problems than it solves.

1. If we consider old templates in old root template directory as Object derivated, they will be shown for all node even if they are not suitable to that node.

The new system ensure that proposed templates can be applied for this node and should not include non existing methods for the node selected.

2. Old template uses % delimited tags which need to be translated.

3. I think very few people are using the old user template. Those could really easily convert their templates ( % => _  and add # meta information if needed) and put it in folders that is suitable for their templates.

> If we consider old templates in old root template directory as Object derivated, they will be shown for all node even if they are not suitable to that node.

They are suitable for all nodes though, just not all objects. Which is why I mentioned both. But since the syntax for placeholders was changed, I guess this is already a compatibility breaking change.

> They are suitable for all nodes though, just not all objects. Which is why I mentioned both. But since the syntax for placeholders was changed, I guess this is already a compatibility breaking change.

What I mean is if someone wrote a template suitable for all Control nodes (template include method calls from Control class) with the old system in the old root directory.

With the new system, we put it in a Control subfolder and it won't be proposed for Node2D or Node3D derivated nodes.

If this template is left in the root template directory and considered to be suitable for all Object, it will kill one of the avdandage of the new system (if a template is proposed, it is suitable).
CharacterBody2D/3D templates are now also available for c# thanks to the reviewers help! The PR is now complete.
@raulsntos Could you confirm now the mono templates work fine now ?
PR meeting: agree this looks good and we want to have this, maintainers/Akien need to figure out last details and then it's merge time :-) Good work!

The list of templates doesn't update when you change the base class. It maybe makes sense on scene, but when you create a script from file system dock you can't use any specific template.

If this was resolved, you could also add a proper template for EditorPlugin (right now it uses some weird special case) and a template for EditorScript.

EDIT:
From what I see, the editor will remember the template per each class. Which means that if you prefer empty template rather than default, you need to change it for every node type you use. That's very inconvenient.

Not sure how could that be improved though. [The preferred template could be remembered for editor](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/1899), but then project-specific templates are a problem.

> Do you just suggest to move the current plugin.gd/cs to EditorPlugin/default.gd to match the other template structure?

Yes. This way we don't have a special case and the template can be used when creating new script from filesystem dock.

> This seems to be saved only when Editor Settings are saved. I think when you confirm script creation and the checkbox state is different than it was before, the settings should automatically save.

I don't think so because someone could prefer empty template for a node type while using another templates for other nodes.
The checkbox will be used for those who don't care about template at all.

> btw what about EditorPlugin/EditorScript? Instead of hard-coded `plugin.gd`, you could use `EditorPlugin/default.gd`.

issue_context.title: EditorPlugins won't let you write "%BASE%"
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:** 3.2.4.rc2
**OS/device including version:** Windows 8.1
**Issue description:**
In my EditorPlugin I wrote the line ``file.replace("%BASE%",sceneRootNode.get_class())`` and whenever I restarted Godot I received the error ``Unable to load addon script from path: 'res://addons/plugin/plugin.gd' There seems to be an error in the code, please check the syntax.``
Attempting to re-enable the addon caused the same error. So I commented out the line but the error persisted.

**Steps to reproduce:**
Create a new plugin with the following lines and then restart Godot:
```
tool
extends EditorPlugin
# %BASE%
```

**Minimal reproduction project:**
[script_templates bug.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/6047115/script_templates.bug.zip)

This bug isn't surprising to see (because of how script_templates work). I'm sure this one's a low priority issue, there are very easy workarounds such as writing "%"+"BASE"+"%". It doesn't seem to affect normal scripts but I haven't checked thoroughly.
comments: cc @Xrayez as they worked on script templates in the past.

Since the script is not parsed, no base type is assigned.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/7bb0d39da4333032d9bb9205ed8d2158692035eb/modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp#L789-L792

Which leads to this:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/7bb0d39da4333032d9bb9205ed8d2158692035eb/editor/editor_node.cpp#L3153-L3157

> cc @Xrayez as they worked on script templates in the past.

Yes, apparently @27thLiz is the one who worked on this based on the git history as well (#9158), so at least need some feedback on how to solve this in the best way possible without introducing hacks.

It may be safe to remove the check and let the script to be parsed, because script templates can be ignored by creating `.gdignore` file if those scripts reside within a project, [which is documented already](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/getting_started/scripting/creating_script_templates.html#language-support-and-overriding-behavior) (referring to #31111 which happens to reveal existing bug).

Could also be possibly solved with annotations in GDScript 2.0 to denote that those script templates are actually templates, and not actual scripts...
